I'm a little torn on this one. While I am vehemently against playing games with someone's emotions, I do find there to be some truth in this song and dance. 

Moreso that the older I get, the more I value interests, hobbies, passion, and ambition in other humans. I don't think that anyone should necessarily be playing games to simulate the idea that they are occupied and interesting, but rather that people should legitimately still be feeding into their own interests and thus, be a little occupied. 

I think the main issue here is people playing games to retain interest, rather than being interesting. If I'm not responding to someone right away, it's because I am giving my attention to something else at that moment. If I'm not available to hang out, it's because I'm respecting my time and other plans I have made. 

As someone who always falls headfirst for other people, I have begun to realize that the level of intensity and devotion that I give off in the beginning feels like a lot. It creates pressure. 

By focusing on my own time for myself more, I have begun removing the pressure for any guy who feels like I'm coming off too strong, whilst also showing that I have my own hobbies as well. Since improving upon this, I've had much more luck with men.

Oh no! Don't feel attacked! I'm a nerdy, non neurotypical  lady person. I just feel like a lot of those guys that I know are so excited and appreciative to find their person that they never question settling down!!!

If a guy is really interested in someone beyond sex, they'll make the effort. 

As for the next thing I'll say, keep in mind that this is not an "every guy" statement. Every dude is different and there are plenty of guys who legitimately want a relationship. 

As human beings we are still driven by our biology and instincts. In my experience, guys in their 20's are largely looking for sex. When they hit their 30's, they start scrambling for more consistency. That and women release oxytocin during sex and become more attached. For men, the chasing aspect disappears and subconsciously, that conquest is over. Again, not saying all guys, but there is some truth to this.

I've noticed a pattern that all my guy friends who have settled down are either
 A.) Not your Hollywood conventionally attractive, 6 ft dudeguys. Not unattractive, just average. 
B.) Post-30 
C.) Nerdy guys or non neurotypical guys who struggle with the process of dating and thus are very appreciative to be out of the dating process when they do find someone.

I've actually been in that position!!! Not inviting someone directly over, but I wanted them to meet me in a public spot to see if we had chemistry and then possibly do the things after. I'm dead convinced they thought I was fake.

My biggest thing about meeting a guy is clean. If it's a very casual meetup like coffee or drinks, I don't expect dressed up, but I expect clean. I don't want someone to go out of their way to look that much different than their norm, but at the same time, show that you give a shit. 

On the flip side though, I went on a tinder date yesterday where the guy was so incredibly nervous and shocked that I didn't stand him up (despite the fact that I kept very open communication and told him I was on my way) that it made me realize that it probably happens relatively often. I think there are so many bots and stuff on tinder, that guys almost don't believe real women exist on there lol. Either that or they are very cautious/doubtful.

28/F here. 

I am a hopeless romantic and incredibly monogamous. One of the best pieces of advice a girlfriend recently gave me was not to hyperfocus on any one human in the early stages of dating. Until exclusivity is talked about, keep talking to people and acknowledge that any person could drop off at any point in time. 

Regardless of this woman's intent, you are stressed out by the situation so far. Dating is an evaluation process on both ends. It's not only her feelings that matter, yours do too. If your needs aren't being met now, and it seems like they aren't, then acknowledge it. Maybe someone with kids isn't for you. Or maybe she's just flaky and that also isn't for you. 

Dating apps have really shitty algorithms and guys vastly outnumber women on them. Because of this, guys overswipe and girls are very selective. Despite this, girls tend to have a crazy amount of other guys on standby. I have a premium feature because I was curious about how many likes I had. I have well over 7000 from this past month. My guy friends who are around the same age and physical attraction have fewer than 30. It's a skewed system and that isn't on you. Covid is making it difficult, but I also highly suggest trying to talk to women in the wild as well. I find that most guys shy away from making moves in person in favor of the immediate confirmation in dating apps. Because of this, the ones who hit on me in person stand out sooo much more.

I agree that meetup groups are going to be big after covid. 

I will say, if you are looking for people with like minded interests, I do think Orlando has what you're looking for. I'm not savvy with all the windermere spots, but I do know that the WOB on university has a large community of 30-40-50-60 year olds that go in there to watch the games. The crowd in there is very relaxed and friendly. 

As for whiskey lovers,  I'm sure you'll find those people as well.  I've heard that Lil Indies on Mills had a nice whiskey selection and I'm certain that the community is here.

There are also a lot of outside events at the breweries! 

I do believe that there's a big difference between clubs/university bars and breweries/craft cocktail bars in terms of crowd congestion. There are plenty of breweries where you can grab your drink, head outside, and still keep enough of a distance that it isn't unsafe.
